caption: Point filtering snaps to whichever texel is nearest, while bilinear weights all four by how much a one-texel box around the UV overlaps each.
Each mip level halves the size, so the whole chain adds only about 33 percent, and the GPU picks the level where one texel covers about one pixel.
A 4x4 block of RGBA8 is 512 bits; BC7 stores it in 128 and ASTC 12x12 gets down to 0.89 bits per texel.
Lambert brightness follows the cosine of the angle between N and L and clamps to zero once the light passes behind the surface.
H always sits halfway between L and V, and the highlight peaks when H lines up with N; higher shininess makes the peak narrower.
Each pixel looks up the depth the light saw and is in shadow when it is farther; too little bias gives acne, too much gives peter-panning.
Forward shades every object once per light; deferred writes the G-buffer once and then lights only the pixels each light touches.
Transparent quads must be blended far to near, and every layer covering a pixel shades it again.
Clamping flattens everything above 1.0 into the same white, while a tonemap curve rolls highlights off smoothly.
Eight draw calls cost eight rounds of CPU state setup; one instanced call costs one, with the same GPU work reading per-instance data.
Frame time is the longer bar: a CPU-bound frame leaves the GPU idle, and a GPU-bound frame leaves the CPU waiting.
Immediate-mode GPUs hit DRAM for every triangle; tile-based GPUs shade each tile on-chip and write it out once.
